title: Double complex with exact rows and columns: the two cokernel complexes have isomorphic homology
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $A=(A_{i,j},d,\delta)_{i,j\ge0}$ be a homological double complex of $R$-modules: $R$-modules $A_{i,j}$ ($i,j\ge0$) and $R$-linear maps $d_{i,j}:A_{i,j}\to A_{i-1,j}$ ($i\ge1$) and $\delta_{i,j}:A_{i,j}\to A_{i,j-1}$ ($j\ge1$) with $d_{i-1,j}\circ d_{i,j}=0$, $\delta_{i,j-1}\circ\delta_{i,j}=0$ and $\delta_{i-1,j}\circ d_{i,j}=d_{i,j-1}\circ\delta_{i,j}$ whenever defined. Put $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_j=\operatorname{Coker}(d_{1,j}:A_{1,j}\to A_{0,j})$ and $A^{\mathrm{up}}_i=\operatorname{Coker}(\delta_{i,1}:A_{i,1}\to A_{i,0})$; the maps $\delta_{0,j}$ induce $R$-linear maps $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_j\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{j-1}$ and the maps $d_{i,0}$ induce $R$-linear maps $A^{\mathrm{up}}_i\to A^{\mathrm{up}}_{i-1}$, which make $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ and $A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet$ chain complexes of $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Assume (1) every row is exact in positive degrees: for all $j\ge0$ and $i\ge1$ the sequence $A_{i+1,j}\xrightarrow{d}A_{i,j}\xrightarrow{d}A_{i-1,j}$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]; (2) every column is exact in positive degrees: for all $i\ge0$ and $j\ge1$ the sequence $A_{i,j+1}\xrightarrow{\delta}A_{i,j}\xrightarrow{\delta}A_{i,j-1}$ is exact. Then for every $n\ge0$ there is an $R$-linear isomorphism $\theta^A_n:H_n(A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$. It is functorial: if $B$ is a second double complex satisfying (1) and (2) and $\Phi:A\to B$ is a morphism of double complexes ($R$-linear maps $\Phi_{i,j}:A_{i,j}\to B_{i,j}$ commuting with $d$ and with $\delta$), and $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}:A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet\to B^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$, $\Phi^{\mathrm{up}}:A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet\to B^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet$ are the induced morphisms of complexes, then $H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})\circ\theta^A_n=\theta^B_n\circ H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{up}})$ for every $n$.

proof.text: Transposition. Let $A^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}=A_{q,p}$, $d^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}=\delta_{q,p}:A^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}\to A^{\mathsf T}_{p-1,q}$, $\delta^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}=d_{q,p}:A^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}\to A^{\mathsf T}_{p,q-1}$. Then $d^{\mathsf T}d^{\mathsf T}=\delta\delta=0$, $\delta^{\mathsf T}\delta^{\mathsf T}=dd=0$ and $\delta^{\mathsf T}_{p-1,q}d^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}=d_{q,p-1}\delta_{q,p}=\delta_{q-1,p}d_{q,p}=d^{\mathsf T}_{p,q-1}\delta^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}$, so $A^{\mathsf T}$ is a double complex. Row $q$ of $A^{\mathsf T}$ is column $q$ of $A$, so hypothesis (2) for $A$ says that every row of $A^{\mathsf T}$ is exact in positive degrees. $(A^{\mathsf T})^{\mathrm{rt}}_p=\operatorname{Coker}(d^{\mathsf T}_{1,p})=\operatorname{Coker}(\delta_{p,1})=A^{\mathrm{up}}_p$, with differential induced by $\delta^{\mathsf T}_{0,p}=d_{p,0}$: $(A^{\mathsf T})^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet=A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet$ as complexes. Identify $T_n(A^{\mathsf T})=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A_{q,p}$ with $T_n(A)$ by $a^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}=a_{q,p}$. The zig-zag condition for $A^{\mathsf T}$, $d^{\mathsf T}(a^{\mathsf T}_{p,q})=\delta^{\mathsf T}(a^{\mathsf T}_{p-1,q+1})$, reads $\delta_{q,p}(a_{q,p})=d_{q+1,p-1}(a_{q+1,p-1})$, which is the zig-zag condition for $A$ at the place $(q+1,p-1)$; so $Z_n(A^{\mathsf T})=Z_n(A)$. Likewise $D^{\mathsf T}_{n+1}(b)_{p,q}=\delta_{q,p+1}(b_{q,p+1})+d_{q+1,p}(b_{q+1,p})=D_{n+1}(b)_{q,p}$, so $B_n(A^{\mathsf T})=B_n(A)$ and $\mathbf H_n(A^{\mathsf T})=\mathbf H_n(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. A morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ gives the morphism $\Phi^{\mathsf T}$ ($\Phi^{\mathsf T}_{p,q}=\Phi_{q,p}$) with $(\Phi^{\mathsf T})^{\mathrm{rt}}=\Phi^{\mathrm{up}}$ and $\mathbf H_n(\Phi^{\mathsf T})=\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$. In Lean, indexSwap exchanges the coordinates, totalSwap is DirectSum.lequivCongrLeft, totalSwap_cycles checks the adjacent equations, and totalSwap_boundary checks the boundary map on direct-sum generators (the two summands exchange places). Restrict with LinearEquiv.ofSubmodules and descend with Submodule.Quotient.equiv. totalSwap_naturality checks coordinatewise maps on the same generators; quotient representative induction gives exists_flipZigzagIso. No exactness or separate zigzagModule_functorial theorem is required for this identification. The quotient map zigzagMap uses zigzagTotalMap_preserves, the preservation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module-functorial], through its definition; this existing proof dependency remains, although the larger conjunction theorem is not invoked.

proof.text: $\rho^A_n$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-to-row-cokernel-map] there is the $R$-linear map $\rho^A_n:\mathbf H_n(A)\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$, $[a]\mapsto[\pi_n(a_{0,n})]$. Surjective: a class in $H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$ is represented by a cycle $y\in A^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$; as $\pi_n$ is onto, $y=\pi_n(x)$ with $x\in A_{0,n}$; by hypothesis (1) and [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-row-cycle-lifts-to-zigzag] there is $a\in Z_n(A)$ with $a_{0,n}=x$, and $\rho^A_n[a]=[y]$. Injective: if $\rho^A_n[a]=0$ then $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$ is a boundary, i.e. lies in $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]; by hypothesis (1) and [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-trivial-if-row-boundary] $a\in B_n(A)$, so $a\in Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A)$ and $[a]=0$. Hence $\rho^A_n$ is an $R$-linear bijection, an isomorphism.

proof.text: The column side. By step 1, $A^{\mathsf T}$ is a double complex whose rows are exact in positive degrees, with $(A^{\mathsf T})^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet=A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet$ and $\mathbf H_n(A^{\mathsf T})=\mathbf H_n(A)$. Step 2 applied to $A^{\mathsf T}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-to-row-cokernel-map], [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-row-cycle-lifts-to-zigzag], [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-trivial-if-row-boundary] for $A^{\mathsf T}$) gives the $R$-linear isomorphism $\lambda^A_n:=\rho^{A^{\mathsf T}}_n:\mathbf H_n(A)\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet)$, $[a]\mapsto[\text{image of }a_{n,0}\text{ in }A^{\mathrm{up}}_n]$.

proof.text: Definition of $\theta$. Put $\theta^A_n=\rho^A_n\circ(\lambda^A_n)^{-1}:H_n(A^{\mathrm{up}}_\bullet)\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$, a composite of $R$-linear isomorphisms (steps 2 and 3), hence an $R$-linear isomorphism. Explicitly: lift a cycle of $A^{\mathrm{up}}_n$ to $a_{n,0}\in A_{n,0}$, complete it to a zig-zag $(a_{n,0},\dots,a_{0,n})$, and take the class of $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$.

proof.text: Use the natural endpoint-map family from [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-to-row-cokernel-map]. Its representative formula and naturality give the naturality square for the row isomorphisms constructed in step 2. Apply that square to the flipped morphism to obtain the column-side square. The coordinate-swap square is proved directly in step 1 from [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Cancel the column-side isomorphism to obtain the square for its inverse, then compose the three squares. Associativity proves the displayed naturality for theta. Neither identity/composition of zigzagMap nor the larger zigzagModule_functorial conjunction is used.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence, algebra.tex 18397-18522) and the setup of R(A), U(A) (18352-18395); tag verified in tags/tags. No Mathlib declaration states it (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep recorded on the node and the new nodes: Mathlib has HomologicalComplex₂ and its total complex but no exactness/quasi-isomorphism statement for bicomplexes); slopmaster2 has no declaration for it (grep by id, 00M1, zig-zag, no-spectral-sequence); its FromJoel/Algebra/Homology/BicomplexColumns.lean has HomologicalComplex₂.total.quasiIso_map_of_isStrictlyGE_of_isStrictlyLE (total of a column-wise quasi-isomorphism of bounded Z-indexed cochain bicomplexes is a quasi-isomorphism), which is a different statement and would replace the source's route, so not attached. Split following the proof of 00M1: the zig-zag module H_n(A) (new definition), the canonical map to H_n(R(A)) with well-definedness and naturality (new, no exactness needed), surjectivity as a lifting lemma and injectivity as a triviality lemma (new, rows exact), and the U(A) side obtained by transposing the double complex (written out in step 1; Z_n and B_n are literally the same for A and its transpose), so only the row side is a node. Statement kept. Source errors (minor): (i) 00M1 describes the trivial zig-zags as generated by $(0,\dots,0,-\delta(a),d(a),0,\dots,0)$; with the source's commuting squares such a tuple is not a zig-zag ($d(-\delta a)\ne\delta(d a)$ in general); the correct generators are $(\dots,\delta(b),d(b),\dots)$, which is what the source's displayed quotient $d(a_{i+1,0})+\delta(a_{i,1}),\dots$ gives; the definition node uses the displayed form. (ii) In the injectivity paragraph the source writes $\operatorname{Coker}(A_{i,1}\to A_{i,0})$ and $\delta:\operatorname{Coker}(A_{i+1,1}\to A_{i+1,0})\to\dots$ where $R(A)_i=\operatorname{Coker}(A_{1,i}\to A_{0,i})$ and $R(A)_{i+1}$ are meant (indices transposed). Neither affects the statement.

lean.statement: theorem doubleComplexCokernelHomologyIso (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : let D := HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) let E := fun A : D => (∀ (p q : ℕ), 0 < p → (ShortComplex.mk ((A.d (p + 1) p).f q) ((A.d p (p - 1)).f q) (by rw [← HomologicalComplex.comp_f, A.d_comp_d, HomologicalComplex.zero_f])).Exact) ∧ (∀ (p q : ℕ), 0 < q → (ShortComplex.mk ((A.X p).d (q + 1) q) ((A.X p).d q (q - 1)) (by simp)).Exact) let flip := flipFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) ∃ θ : ∀ (A : D), E A → ∀ n : ℕ, (A.flip.opcycles 0).homology n ≅ (A.opcycles 0).homology n, ∀ (A B : D) (hA : E A) (hB : E B) (Φ : A ⟶ B) (n : ℕ), (θ A hA n).hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (HomologicalComplex.opcyclesMap Φ 0) n = HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (HomologicalComplex.opcyclesMap (flip.map Φ) 0) n ≫ (θ B hB n).hom
